plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks losses if you win at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since values are private and independent, the optimal strategy is straightforward truth-telling: bid exactly my value of $25, ensuring maximum expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. Bidding above value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing an item you'd have profited from. With a value of $3, I should bid exactly $3 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey-style) with 3 bidders and independent private values drawn uniformly from [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since the price paid depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $26.
